utterances.text: All right. A moment ago, you said that their vehicles were seized and their food was seized and all the rest of it, all the other things you mentioned. Now, Mr. Nice presented you this morning with your tab, tab 1.35, where he claimed that from a quotation towards the end of the statement it would emerge that a certain person provided food to the KLA and that they assisted them in that way. So I'm going to read out that quotation from the statement so that we can see whether it was somebody who provided food or whether there was any other functions that person performed. And this is what it says in tab 1.35, the tab mentioned by Mr. Nice a moment ago, but he didn't go on to quote from the document. It says the following here: "To the locals of the village of Racak, in the houses --" I'm not going into the exactitude of the Serbian language here, but anyway: "Bajrami Ragip came to the houses of the villages of Racak and he ordered each of the households what food they should provide and supply and then he would take the food and take it away." Now, this individual who went from house to house, to each of the households, ordering them what they were to supply, is this considered to be somebody who provided food or was this an official representative of the KLA doing the work he was doing as is stated here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, he was a member of the KLA because he was with the KLA and in addition to the staffs of the KLA the civilian defence was set up too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But I'm taking this critical word. It says: "Who to every household would order which foodstuffs were required." So who is it who would be in a position to issue orders to households?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nobody can order anybody anything. What we're dealing with here is the fact that the KLA ordered the local inhabitants, specifically of this particular village, what they were to do, not only to provide food but also to provide money for the purchase of weapons and other needs, over requirements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So this person issuing orders on the part of the KLA, must he have been a member of the KLA performing this function?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course. That would be quite normal and natural, because apart from the KLA who else would there be? What other organisation or political party would be able to issue orders like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So was his primary activity, the fact that he provided food for the KLA or that he went from house to house ordering the inhabitants what they were supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the meeting itself, the meeting that took place in the mosque, the villagers were ordered to come up with money and foodstuffs and everything else that the KLA needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Was that the reason for which most of the inhabitants moved out of the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was one of the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, to go back to the questions that had to do with whether a written report existed or didn't exist about what actually happened in Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we reach that position and just for clarification, the previous answer on the question of families moving out referred to notes which the witness says he had. Now, it may be, and I've been trying to track it down over the last couple of minutes, it may be that the notes he refers to as existing in December 1998 showing that 10 to 15 families stayed in Racak are some of the statements we've got here, but I can't immediately remember which ones. If not, then he's referring to other documents that haven't been made available to us yet. It's on line 25 of page 44. That's all right. We've found it. Well, I've found one reference, and it would appear to be 1.35 again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Your point is what, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: My point was to know what the witness was referring to when he was referring to notes, but it appears he may be referring to 1.35, in which case we have the material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, we're dealing with facts here, and I was asking the witness how many inhabitants the village of Racak had, and his answer was between 2 to 3.000. At the time of the police operation in Racak, you yourself were able to see that there were several dozen. So that makes it about 1 per cent of the 2 to 3.000, or 1.5 per cent perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's your next question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's take a look at the binder prepared by Mr. Nice about Racak. I don't have time to dwell on all the papers that binder contains, but let us now take a look at tab 5, for instance, which he provided, and I'm very pleased to see that we finally have an authentic document which was not placed at my disposal, I didn't have at my disposal. Would you please take a look at tab 5.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't got that tab in front of me, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let it be passed to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, it is not true that he has not -- he had not this one at his disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour is absolutely right. It was an exhibit provided by Eric Baccard, tab 16 of Exhibit 156 and separately produced, I think, as tab 27 of 320. The only thing that's new about tab 5 is the particular translation, I think, because there were -- there were more than one version of the translation in existence. And I read from and therefore relied upon the official translation which has the ERN number 03046070 in the top right-hand corner rather than earlier and draft translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have that dispatch now before you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, dated the 15th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. All right. So the date is the date of the event in Racak. Does it say on top "The Ministry of the Interior, Urosevac, number 402/98." The date is the 15th of January, 1999, Urosevac. Is that the date when the event in Racak took place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's when the events in the village of Racak occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when Walker came to Racak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really remember when he came.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who was this dispatch sent to? Let us first take a look at who signed it. At the very end on page 3, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The then chief of SUP, Colonel Bogoljub Janicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So he sends a report to the ministry. The chief of SUP sends a report to the ministry. The SUP of Urosevac, does it have territorial jurisdiction over this location in Racak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It is stated here that it is also sent to the administration of the criminal investigation department.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is whether they have territorial jurisdiction over Racak.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because Racak belongs to Stimlje and Stimlje comes under the jurisdiction of the SUP in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Who was this dispatch sent to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the Ministry of the Interior, Republic of Serbia, criminal -- administration of the criminal investigation department, the operative operations centre in Belgrade, as well as the MUP staff for Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So the chief of the secretariat in Urosevac sends a dispatch to the Ministry, to the administration of the criminal investigation department, to the police administration, to the operations centre, and to the MUP staff in Kosovo and Metohija, which is located in Pristina. All right. Now, let us see what is stated here. What do it say in the very beginning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Overview of events, phenomena, and activities in the Urosevac SUP on the 15th of January, 1999, from 0300 hours to 1830 hours on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Read on.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 15th of January, 1999, in 0300 hours, the village of Racak, Stimlje municipality, was blocked off in order to capture and destroy a terrorist group concerning which we had information that in the territory covered by Urosevac SUP it carried out a number of terrorist attacks with lethal consequences. At 06 -- at 6.30 in the morning, the village was placed under siege by the team of Urosevac SUP. On the left side of the road, the Siptar terrorist gangs opened fire from a rocket launcher and infantry weapons. The fire was responded to. The terrorists withdrew before the police advancement, constantly firing at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fight with the terrorists went on until 1530 hours, and from the village the policemen were shot at from the Browning 12.7 millimetres and from mortars. The terrorist group was attacked -- was liquidated with the maximum effort on the part of the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it's time for a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, is it stated here what was the objective when the police entered Racak? What does it say in the second passage after the words "Stimlje municipality"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The first passage has only two lines, and then the second passage.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 15th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to capture and destroy the terrorist group concerning which --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Concerning which. We have all that information. Further on does it say that from the direction of Stimlje, which is the direction from which the police entered the village, the terrorist -- terrorists opened fire at police members?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. From a location called Cesta. We had information concerning that earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about that. All I'm asking you is is it stated here that as the police entered the area it was fired at?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from a rocket -- hand-held rocket launcher and infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Was it clear to everyone that there was a KLA terrorist group in Racak?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you know very well these questions beginning "Was it clear" end up as leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, as the Court will appreciate, having no other witness to deal with the investigation, I did elicit through this witness answers on what the material revealed to a policeman. So I don't, of course, seek to deny the opportunity to the accused to re-examine on that basis, but any re-examination on the basis of the facts in light of his expressed ignorance this morning of matters beyond the narrow remit he says he and Sparavalo had might be not justified, but it's obviously a delicate matter and I'll leave it to the good judgement of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, I will now show you -- or, rather, quote to you only a segment of the testimony of Shukri Buja here, which is on page 6366 of the transcript. He testified on Thursday, the 6th of June, 2002. So on page 6366 --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's right. You don't have it. I will read it out to you. Everybody else here has it, has the document. He was asked about the number of soldiers, as they call them here, the soldiers of the KLA. And in line 3 they say: "[In English] Yes, it is true that there were 47 soldiers in the positions near Racak." [Interpretation] On the following page, Judge May ask: "[In English] Just a minute, if you're going to make allegations of that sort one by one. First of all, did you show the investigator your base or headquarters in Racak?" [Interpretation] And then the witness -- "[In English] The

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the following page, 6372, he mentions Mehmet Mustafa. And then in line 17 says: "[In English] [Previous translation continues] ... soldier for KLA." [Interpretation] Do you remember that name, Mehmet Mustafa from your notes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that name, Mehmet Mustafa, because it appears in a number of statements and Official Notes. I also remember that in his house there was a substaff of the KLA in the village of Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to what is mentioned in the report of the chief of the secretariat, dated the 15th of January, namely that they opened fire, at the bottom of the page 6381 it is stated: "[In English] During the Serbian assault from Cesta and the burst of gunfire from the 12.7 from the bunker, they started -- started filing out of the base at Racak gorge and outside the house Mehmet Mustafa and Sadik Mujota were killed. Beqa and Nazim Kokollari which was also known as Budakovc. Some soldiers managed to move towards our position. They faced the Serbian fire." [Interpretation] And then they mention Mujota Mustafa, Syla Kadri, Nazim Kokollari, Ali Beqa, Skender Jashari. Mr. Jasovic, based on the testimony of Shukri Buja, is it clear that as the police entered Racak it was fired upon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, "Is it clear that." Again, leading. I think you're perfectly capable of putting proper questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, as the police entered the village of Racak, who opened fire based on everything that you have learned so far?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The witness can't deal with that. He's already said he doesn't know the facts. He barely knows the documents. He had a very narrow remit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't think you're going to be helped by that answer, Mr. Milosevic. Ultimately the Chamber will have to decide that matter. We have the evidence before us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, Mr. Robinson, as the witness was asked several times whether there were any written reports back at the time when the event was concluded, let us just see what is stated in this dispatch. The encryption is not that important. PC131/19/152, and then this says time 1952 and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So at 1952 on that day, the chief of the Secretariat of the Interior sent a report to the ministry, to the administration of the criminal investigation department, to the police administration, and to the operations centre with a brief description of everything that took place. Is it something that can be seen based on this document or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see here that the dispatch was sent on the same day at 1952.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. All those various photographs, claims as to where the corpses were found, what happened and everything else that you saw, do you know when those photographs were made? When was that filmed? When was that established?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photographs are not familiar to me at all. I don't know when they were taken or distributed to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, may I ask you whether this is the only report of the Racak incident of which you are aware?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In addition to this report, several days ago I was able to see the chronology of the events in the village of Racak, just several days ago. I don't know. I didn't really study the Racak case, the documentation starting with the on-site report and investigation and so on, except for the fact that I conducted operative work in order to shed light not only on what happened in Racak but also other cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In the normal course of events, is it the chief of the SUP, the colonel, who would be the person to make such a report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Either the chief of the SUP or if so designated by him it could be either the chief of the criminal investigation department or somebody else. However, in this particular case I don't know who wrote this dispatch. It is not really for me to know who wrote this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, you misunderstood the question. However, I will try to clarify it for you. Is there a territorial, an organisational unit above the Secretariat of the Interior when it comes to territorial jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the SUP was in Urosevac, the base, the main office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. The SUP in Urosevac. So any other SUP in the territory of the Republic of Serbia, do they directly report to the ministry as is stated here in this report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the chief of the secretariat naturally reports to the establishment above him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, in this case, in the territorial and organisational sense, what institution comes above the secretariat in Urosevac here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the secretariat in Pristina in the Ministry of the Interior in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. The chief of the secretariat in Urosevac, is he the superior in that organ and in that territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the secretariat covers the territory of Strpce, Stimlje, and Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Yes, we know that. Between the secretariat and the ministry, is there a unit in between these two?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now that you've mentioned this chronology which can be found in tab 33 of Mr. Nice and could also be found in the judgements of General Stevanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we are moving off, while we are staying on this tab 5, Mr. Jasovic, my colleague Judge Bonomy raised this issue some days ago. This dispatch is saying that seven prisoners were taken into custody to be interviewed on the issue of terrorism and were turned over for further work to the authorised officials of Urosevac SUP and DB of Urosevac. What I find very odd or even unreliable with respect to your answer in this regard is that it should be you who should have interviewed these seven people, but your answer is that you don't just -- you don't remember it. You said you don't remember the names of these people, but what is important is not whether -- not whether you remember the names of those people but whether those seven people were ever turned in for that interview.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said, because it's been over six years, that I cannot remember. These persons were perhaps handed over to the state security sector on the fourth floor. I really cannot remember. There is no reason. If they had been interviewed by me, I would have said so. Possibly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. If these seven people were interviewed by you, I see no reason for you not to remember the fact, because that Racak incident is so -- so important one. It's very -- so heated debate was going on on the Racak incident. So I don't see any -- there could be any reason for you not to remember it. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know, Your Honour. I would have told you the names and surnames, really, of these people, but I cannot remember. It's been six and a half years. I cannot remember. Perhaps I was not the one who interviewed them. It was members of the state security sector who also processed such individuals. I don't know. There's probably a report sent to the duty service or, rather, by the duty service in terms of where these individuals were sent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. I don't think I can get further than that. Proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kwon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This sentence that Mr. Kwon referred to is towards the very top of the last page of this report. Can you read it out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "For the purpose of an interview related to terrorism, seven persons were brought in, and they were handed over for further processing to the OSL in Urosevac and the ODB in Urosevac. Am I supposed to read it further on?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No, that's all.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, SDB not ODB.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says seven persons were brought in for an interview. Is that what it says there, Mr. Jasovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says that seven persons were brought in for an interview. And that they were handed over to officials, authorised officials of the SUP of Urosevac and the ORDB in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, with regard to each and every individual that you interviewed, every friendly contact you had, any person who was brought in or came of his own free will, did you write up the person's interview or an Official Note?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally. A statement was taken and a note was compiled or another information document. Now, what it says here, I mean, I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not forcing you to say anything that you don't know, Mr. Jasovic. I just asked you very specifically whether in every case when you interview an individual, for example, in this kind of case when a person is brought in to you for an interview in respect of terrorism.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Would you compile a note about that or would it happen that you would not compile a note about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could not happen because the person had been brought in and then most probably I would take a statement from the said individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So you'd take -- you'd take a statement. If this statement had been taken, would it have to be among the statements of yours that were presented here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you identify any of these persons among these statements? Was there anyone that you interviewed on the 16th, 17th, 18th? Have you got any such individuals?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th and on the 17th, I remember because now as I looked through this documentation I saw that, but I cannot remember anything about the 15th. Had I taken a statement or compiled a note then, it would probably have to be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you help us with this, what it is that you have here from the 16th or the 17th? Had these persons been brought to you in the evening of the 15th, that is to say before 1952 when the document was compiled? Would you have interviewed them that same night or tomorrow morning or when? I'm asking about your practice.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not only practice, because there was no suspicion -- specific suspicion why this person would be detained had this person not taken part in any kind of terrorist action. So once a person like that is interviewed, the person is released. That is to say, the said person goes home. And if the person is brought in on the 15th, then the interviews would be conducted with all the persons on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Among these statements, do you have any that pertain to the 16th, for instance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, because I remember that the Prosecutor put this to me in relation to Afrim Mustafa. I can't remember now. I can't remember the other names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shaban Rama.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I'd have a look at the documents, I think it was for three or four persons that the Prosecutor mentioned this to me. Was it Emini Shemsi?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Jasovic. In these documents of yours that you submitted, I'm going to ask you about them in individually, because I assume that this can pertain only to them if they were with you. You say that perhaps they were, perhaps they weren't.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says on the top of the page when the person was brought in and when the interview was conducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not sure that the accused isn't by one strategy or another trying to lead. There's nothing in these materials I think either produced by the witness or the material on which I cross-examined to suggest being taken in on the 15th, which is what is being suggested in this document dated the 15th. The witness has already said he doesn't know the name of the people who were brought in, and he's been asked that question several times by me and now more recently by Judge Kwon, and to try and force these people who were seen on the 16th and 17th or who were said to have been seen on the 16th and 17th into this bottle is a form of a leading question and it's an exercise that is, in my submission, a waste of time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, this sentence from the report of the head of the SUP says with a view to an interview pertaining to terrorism, seven persons were brought in, that's what it says, and they were handed over for processing to the authorised official of the SUP and the ORDB of Urosevac. So with a view to an interview pertaining to terrorism. Those are the words here. That is a general statement. And that is why I'm asking, in relation to this interview pertaining to terrorism, I have here tab 143, which is dated the 16th of January, was that the interview pertaining to terrorism? That's the question I'm putting to the witness. In document in tab 143 dated the 16th of January --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the interviews.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness says that he doesn't know whether he interviewed precisely one of the individuals mentioned here, but then no one is mentioned by name here. It is only "Interviews pertaining to terrorism" that are mentioned here. My question is whether this interview is an interview pertaining to terrorism.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the dispatch it says interview pertaining to terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And this tab of yours, 1.43, interview pertaining to terrorism. Would that be it now that you look at it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And 1.44, which was also taken on the 16th of January, is that also an interview pertaining to terrorism?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let us not go any further to 17, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the same time, the time coincides. Interviews are conducted in relation to terrorism. The sole assignment that this witness had, as he explained it, was to find out the names and surnames of members of the KLA, their deployment, the weapons they had, and that is what he was doing. He cannot link up the mention of these seven individuals, but we see that on the 16th and on the 17th again there are interviews conducted that pertain to terrorism. There is no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, are you alluding that these witnesses are maybe part of those seven people taken from the scene?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not that I'm suggesting that, but it cannot be excluded altogether. And secondly, it doesn't say that these persons were brought in from the scene. There is different information contained in this dispatch. It just says here that seven persons were brought in for interviews pertaining to terrorism. They could have brought in anywhere. It doesn't say that they were brought in from the scene at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jasovic, do the people in DB, ORDB, take witness statements as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they do. As -- just like members of the public security sector take statements, then it is also members of the state security sector that take interviews from persons or they also compile Official Notes with regard to such interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, go back to the previous page in -- with a view top interviews pertaining to terrorism, seven persons were brought in. It says that on the top of the last page.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does it say in the preceding passage on the previous page? Just read the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "During the night, between the 14th and 15th of January, 1999, members of the police station in Strpce held certain places in Susici and Gornje Bitinje, and during the reporting day the persons who held the mentioned places and the observation points were not attacked by terrorists."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it says that there were no terrorist attacks against members of the police who were at those places. And on the next stage -- on the next page it says seven persons were brought in for questioning about terrorism into the SUP.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in that dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But does it say anything that they were brought in from the scene in Racak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what it says here. It's possible that the police found them somewhere else, in Stimlje or wherever else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. All right. So if you look --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The English translation says that seven persons were taken into custody. Is that an accurate translation from the original document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, it says here: "With a view to interviews pertaining to terrorism, seven persons were brought in." It doesn't say that they were taken into custody. It says that they were brought in, and then the rest follows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you're quite clear that if they were brought in in these circumstances on the 15th, they would be interviewed on the 15th. That was the answer you gave earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You wouldn't have any authority to hold them in custody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if the person is not a suspect, a crime suspect, we cannot keep them in detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These persons were brought in. My opinion is that they were immediately taken for interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When we read this dispatch here, it starts with the following words: "Survey of phenomena, activities of the SUP on the 15th of January, 1999." And then that is great deal about Racak until a paragraph where there is no mention of Racak. Look at this, please, the previous paragraph, the second paragraph on this second page, the second one from the bottom. Can you read that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the 15th of January, 1999, members of the RPO Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Gornje Nerodimlje held two particular positions in the region of Jezerce and members of the SUP Urosevac observation points in the area of the village of Crnoljevo and the Crnoljevo pass."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. These are localities that are not Racak that are mentioned here now.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The village of Jezerce in the area of the village of Crnoljevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But not the village of Racak.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, not that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And now during the night Susici and Bitinje were the places where they held positions. Is that the village of Racak or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They are in the municipality of Stimlje -- or Strpce.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says that there were no terrorist attacks?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And only in the third paragraph it says with regard to interviews pertaining to terrorism a number of individuals are brought in, et cetera. So the subject of Racak is dropped altogether, Jezerce, Crnoljevo, Bitinje are referred to and seven persons are brought in for interviews with regard to terrorism. Are these seven persons linked up to Racak in any way?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says here, "With a view to interviews pertaining to terrorism seven persons were brought in for further processing." I don't know where these persons were brought in from. I could assume --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. All right. Mr. Jasovic, is what the first paragraph of this dispatch says being challenged?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first page --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the first page. You read it out so I don't lead you in any way. Start with the text.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "A review of all events for the 15th of January, between 0300 hours to 1830 hours."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this all refers to Racak except for the last paragraphs before the end which refer to Jezerce, Crnoljevo and so on. And then the next refers to Susici and Bitinje and only the third one after that relates to the seven persons and the interview; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I'm not going to deal with that material anymore sent by the chief the secretariat to a higher authority. You mentioned the chronology of events in tab 33 and Mr. Nice asked you some questions and said whether there were two policemen who intervened. So I'm now going to ask you to take a look at tab 33 yourself. It's the chronology of events. Mr. Nice dwelled on that chronology during his cross-examination for some time. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it. "Events in the village of Racak" it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that the interpreters have the original text. And if not, could they be provided with the original text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the original be passed over to the interpreters. Well, let it be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Place it on the ELMO, please. Just that long first paragraph, because that's the one we're going to be discussing. Can we have the Serbian version as well, please. That's from the Racak binder, tab 33, and the title of the document is "Chronology of the events in the village of Racak." We have it on the overhead projector. I hope that the interpreters can follow this on the ELMO, that they can see and read from the document on the ELMO. If not, then please maybe they -- may they be given a copy, but that depends on them.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We have the Serbian on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, when you see this long first paragraph, and I'm just going to read -- would you just keep focused on the first paragraph with the overhead projector, please, don't move it around. I'm just going to read the beginning and the end of the paragraph, which is one single sentence although it takes up a third of the page, and this is what it says: "With the aim of arresting the terrorist group," that's what it says, the first five words. And then if you skip all the rest of it and come to the one but last line and continue reading, it says: "On the 15th of January, 1999, in the early hours of the morning, an operation was perpetrated with the aim of apprehending and depriving of liberty or arresting the terrorist group in Racak." Now, Mr. Jasovic, everything in between, is that just stating what the terrorist group did?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The fact is that a number of terrorist attacks had previously been carried out in the main road from Stimlje-Crnoljevo and also on the main road of Stimlje running to Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, can we conclude from that, and I'd like to ask the interpreters to look at the paragraph, that that whole sentence, which starts off by saying that the aim was to arrest the terrorist group, now, what are the reasons stated in the middle of the sentence? Does it give a reason? The attack on a vehicle, on an official vehicle with police markings where one policeman was killed. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. An armed attack carried out on a policeman of the SUP of Urosevac, 6624.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Which one police man was killed. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the number is given M 616-424.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And there is another person mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two other men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But it says when Przic Svetislav was lethally wounded, a policeman was lethally wounded, and then an NN criminal report was filed, et cetera. So that is one reason, one of the reasons for the activities in Racak. Now, is another reason mentioned here because of frequent armed attacks on members of the police force and the police station at Stimlje. Is that also what it says? Is that another reason that is mentioned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then it goes to say: "And the kidnapping of a large number of citizens loyal to the Republic of Serbia?" Is that also what it says? Is that another reason, yet another reason?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Kidnap a number of people Serbs, Albanians, Roma, et cetera. Then it says: On the basis of operative information that from the basis of the headquarters of Stimlje in the village of Racak. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So we have here listed four reasons for which the blockade is being perpetrated; the attack on the vehicle where one person was killed; frequent armed attacks on members of the police; third, the kidnapping of a large number of citizens; and, fourth, information about the staff or headquarters in village of Racak, of terrorists in the village of Racak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So all these four reasons, are they enumerated and stipulated as reasons for which the activities in Racak was undertaken?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You have all four reasons stated there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, Mr. Robinson, this is a very unwieldy and lengthy sentence but it is just one sentence, after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, linking up what it says here or, rather, comparing, Mr. Jasovic, what it says here in this chronology with the report that we read out a moment ago about the daily events where 80 per cent of the reports were devoted to Racak sent in by the head of SUP, can we see that what is stipulated coincides or what is said different?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here the allegations and what is stated coincides. They are the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, would you read out on page 2, please, paragraph 4. It begins with the words "prili komna stupanja." [phoen]

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "When the members of the police force arrived in the village of Racak and their efforts to see that the members of the terrorist bands are -- gangs are arrested with an appeal that armed members of the terrorist group should surrender, when this appeal was refused they withdrew from the village of Racak. While firing strongly they withdrew to the village of Ruzica, Rance and Petrovo in the Stimlje municipality, along with heavy fire."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Would you read out the next paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In addition to the fact that they were running after the individuals and appealed to them to surrender, the terrorist groups continued to engage in strong fire. The terrorist attacks the police with great force from previously prepared trenches, communicating trenches and bunkers. In the said exchange of gunfire, 40 Siptar terrorists were liquidated of which the majority were wearing uniforms of the so-called KLA."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Then it goes on to state what was found, what kind of weapons, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, does it say here that all this was found in one location, on one spot, or in several locations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean at the bottom there referring to weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By taking control of the bunkers and trenches used by the terrorists, the members of the police in addition to the said corpses found and confiscated, et cetera, et cetera, in several places.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, does it say they were killed in one locality or in several localities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't read anywhere that it says they died in one place, in one spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nice presented to you a number of photographs and markings where the individuals or bodies were found. Now, to the best of your knowledge, was anybody -- did anybody from the Verification Mission take those photographs and make those markings on that particular day or on some other day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I'm not aware of that. I saw that for the first time when I was shown them, shown these photographs, by the Prosecutor earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, take a look at the following page, paragraph 3, please. We'll just read that out. We don't have time to dwell on this for too long.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean because it says about the impossibility, "spogananucustje." [phoen]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to read it out?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the impossibility of carrying out a comprehensive detailed analysis of the on-site investigation in the village of Racak and because it was impossible to provide security for the spot where the terrorists were liquidated, during the night the 15th and 16th of January, 1999, the said corpses of the terrorists remained accessible to terrorist groups from the village of Petrovo and the village of Malopoljce so that there is the possibility that the terrorists manipulated -- with the liquidated terrorists and changed their clothing into civilian clothing, confiscating their personal ID papers, and the bodies of persons who were not in the area of Stimlje municipality, and that they took away the bodies or in some other way manipulated with the alleged corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Without going into everything that could have happened here, the possibilities of what could have happened, can we say or, rather, from the event up until the time that somebody from outside - and when I say "outside" I mean our investigating organs or the Verification Mission or anybody else came on the spot - did at least 24 hours go by before that occurred, without entering into what they might have done with the bodies or might not have done. We're not challenging that between the event and between anybody turning up on the spot that at least 24 hours elapsed. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: How does the witness know? He wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you in a position to answer that, Mr. Jasovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think I understood the question fully in the first place. Could I be given a --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says here: "During the night between the 15th and 16th," and you read what it says here, "Because it was impossible to provide security for the place where the terrorists were liquidated in the night between the 15th and 16th of January the said corpses were accessible to the terrorists from the village of Petrovo and Malopoljce." So overnight. Was somebody there in except for the member of the KLA? Was anybody else there except for the members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were no police there because the police had withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, do you happen to know when the Verification Mission arrived in Racak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really can't say. I don't know when it arrived exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, we have facts about that, information about that, so it's not contested. But at any event, I'm asking you as a crime inspector yourself, is it possible to manipulate -- would it have been possible to manipulate bodies in the space of 24 hours overnight if they were left there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not by the police but by the KLA members, yes, that was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. I'm not going to deal with that document any more or with these tabs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why by the KLA members but not by the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, because the police had withdrawn. And I'm saying this because when last time I said that I had knowledge and information in addition to the 40 from Schedule A, that there were five other individuals who in the clashes between the Albanian terrorists and the police had been killed. I know that the policemen withdrew, had withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 3 of that same binder, Mr. Nice made a statement for the public -- provided a statement, sorry. Provided a statement. It's in tab 3, Mr. Jasovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tab 3 of what, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This binder on Racak provided by Mr. Nice. It's the binder where it just says "Racak documents" on the binder. "Racak documents" is the title. The same one from which we took tab 5 and tab 33 that we analysed just a little bit ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it not a video segment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is the last page where it says: "Statement for the public." 7.3. A copy of the statement for the public dated the 15th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Tab 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nice. Tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Have you found that, Mr. Jasovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What's the date on the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ministry of the Interior, the 15th of January, 1999, Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was that the date of Racak event?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was when the event in Racak took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is that the same date when the chief of the secretariat reported about the event in Racak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same date, 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And it's stated in this document as well.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please read out just the first several lines.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the 15th of January, 1999, the police took measures in order to block the village of Racak, Stimlje municipality, in order to locate and arrest members of the terrorist group."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No need to read further on because it lists their activities and so on. They killed seven members of an Albanian community and so on. Just read the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Member of this" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Kosovo Verification Mission of the OSCE was informed about the measures taken. Their information service was informed."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will not dwell on this any longer because it is very time-consuming. Now, I will follow the order of the questions put to you by Mr. Nice concerning which I made notes. In the beginning of the cross-examination, Mr. Nice showed you a report about torture, or perhaps he just mentioned that report. I have to apologise to both of you for not noting that down accurately, but it concerns the torture of a young man in 1994. Do you remember any kind of torture taking place in your police station or in the Secretariat of the Interior at any time and particularly in 1994, because this is what you were asked about.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember anything about that event, that case. In addition to that, I have no information indicating that any torture took place in the Secretariat of the Interior in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Jasovic. Urosevac is not a very large city, is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think it has about 70.000 residents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. How many people worked in the Secretariat of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't give you the exact number, the total.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I mean the building itself. I don't mean the entire territory under the jurisdiction of the secretariat, because it covers four municipalities. I just mean the building, the building of the Secretariat of the Interior. How many people approximately?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five to 600. I'm not sure. I'm not even sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When I ask how many people worked in the building, I don't mean the policemen who were beat policemen, who were in patrols and so on. I just mean how many people had offices in the building of the Urosevac SUP.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, 100, 200. Once again, I'm not sure. This is an approximation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. All of these questions that I put to you have just one single purpose. Mr. Jasovic, if such an incident did indeed take place, torture of people and so on, would you have known about it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, because I started working in 1975. That was when I was first employed by the Secretariat of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Nice said here that Serbia was a police state where torture was administered, where police abused their authority. I'm not quite sure how he termed that, but at any rate, he used the phrases indicating that a large number of unlawful activities took place. He quoted the reports of the Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, and so on.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Serbia was not a police state.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I will put now on the overhead projector the report of the Human Rights Watch. Let me just explain to you what it is about. I will put it on the ELMO in order to ask you whether some of such cases took place in Urosevac or in some other police stations in Serbia. I will give you Human Rights Watch report for 1998, which pertains to 14 cities in the United States. So this is a report of the Human Rights Watch for the United States in 1998. That was the year when, according to Mr. Nice, you engaged in torture, beating, and so on. It was even mentioned that somebody died in the police station. All right. I will ask the usher to put this on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What do you intend to put, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to put on the ELMO the Human Rights Watch report pertaining to 14 cities in the United States in 1998. This report discusses torture, murder, and specific cases. I want to ask the witness whether anything similar occurred in Serbia, whether he has any knowledge of such cases taking place in Serbia. And then I want to ask him about the Amnesty International report pertaining to Germany and analysing police abuse; and then Great Britain, again police abuse; France, police abuse and so on. I want to ask him Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. whether anything similar took place in Serbia, because Mr. Nice brought here Human Rights Watch report detailing how somebody was killed in a police station in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's not relevant --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well. Very well, Mr. Robinson. It doesn't even need to be relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, just on one matter before I lose sight of it, you were asked about the incident in 1994, which is relevant, and this was an alleged incident of torture in the offices -- well, in the building of the Urosevac SUP. And you were asked a question: "If such an incident did indeed take place, torture of people and so on, would you have known about it?" And your answer was, "Yes, certainly, because I started working in 1975." Now, is that your position, that if an incident of torture of any kind took place within that building you would know about it? Because that was not your position last week.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I'm saying is this: If there was some grave incident, I probably would have learned about that from my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue, Mr. Bonomy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, I will broaden the scope of my question. Had such a case really took place? I'm not asking you whether you would know about that, but, rather, do you think that the entire Urosevac would have -- would know about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. Not just about a major case. Even a minor case would become known throughout the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: A case of that nature where somebody was killed or tortured in a police station in such a small town as Urosevac, can something like that be concealed at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's impossible to conceal something like that, that somebody was killed in a police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Were you not asked about an incident in which a man was thrown from the fourth floor and died and you said you didn't know of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I'm saying now, that I don't know of such a case. And that's what I answered when the question was put to me. I probably would have heard about it had there really been such a case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, where is the building of the Secretariat of the Interior in Urosevac? Is it in the centre of Urosevac? Is it on the outskirts, in an isolated place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is outside of the centre of Urosevac in the direction of Stimlje near the railroad tracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How many --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we are well past the time for the break. We will adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, yesterday Mr. Nice showed you a photograph of Racak and two lists of names. I will ask the usher to put this on the overhead projector. One has a list of names, many of which are marked green, which means that they are mentioned in your documents as members of the KLA, whereas the other one is a list of names of persons who were in a house and not mentioned any further, and allegedly those who are not mentioned any further remained alive. Put this on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, since I was unable to find it anywhere, would Mr. Nice be able to tell us based on which -- based on what he claims that the people whose names are marked in green are the people who were in Racak during the events. Where did he acquire that information and based on what is he claiming that these people were in Racak?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether that is a matter for Mr. Nice to --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. But as a matter of assistance for the accused, he will find that the evidence source is dealt with at the top of each list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So the marked ones are those who appear in the statements taken by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Sorry, yes. The highlighting is all -- what it is the accused -- derives from what it is the accused wants to put in by way of exhibits. The evidential source for the general proposition that these were the people who were killed in Racak is part of our evidence, and the source of that is shown at the head of the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not what I asked, Mr. Robinson. The names on the list on the left, which can be found in the exhibits provided by Mr. Jasovic or for Mr. Jasovic, I know the sources for these names because the source is in the interviews collected by Mr. Jasovic as an authorised official. What I'm interested in is the list on the right. Mr. Nice claims that these are the people who managed to escape. Based on what is he claiming that these people were in Racak at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I correct the position because I couldn't see because of the size of the type on the screen. I thought that it had actually been added to the list but in fact it was a handwritten note for me. The source of the material on the right is Exhibit 174, which is Drita Emini's statement, and it's pages 11 to 12 of that. I think actually I read that out last week. The source of the material on the left is Exhibits 209, pages 4 to 5 of that Exhibit, and also Exhibit 187, pages 2 to 3 of that. But the accused's immediate concern is met by Exhibit 174.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So there you have it, Mr. Milosevic. Exhibit 174, pages 11 to 12.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. That means that the statement of a witness is the basis for claiming that these civilians were in Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, do you know anything about group which was in Racak and allegedly left Racak in the course of this police operation on the 15th of January, 1999?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the interviews conducted, I have no such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In that case, we will not need the list which is on the ELMO now any longer. Mr. Jasovic, based on the comparison which was made here, in relation to 30 persons, which can be found in Schedule A of Mr. Nice, you noted down in your statements that they were members of the KLA. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that, and what I stated is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I have a list with 30 names here. Based on the statements, if you're able to tell us that, that's fine. If not, we'll go back to your statements. So in relation to persons which can be found on Schedule A of Mr. Nice, before the 15th, in the statements collected by you, how many of these persons based on your work were members of the KLA? What were you able to establish?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have information concerning 14 persons indicating that they were members of the KLA before the event in Racak, that is to say before the 15th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Would you be able to show us now in which of your documents the persons mentioned there are -- appear as well? Let us start with Rexhep Bajrami -- Ragip Bajrami. Would we be able to establish that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we would. I just need to see the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Based on what my associates were able to find, his name is mentioned in tabs 1.35, 1.50, 1.51, and 1.54, that is to say in four statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, whether this arises from cross-examination I don't know. The scheduling of this material ought to have been done in chief but wasn't. We've done it on the chart which we've made to be as inclusive as we possibly can, even to include people who shouldn't be there at all, and if there is any challenge to the chart's accuracy the Chamber might find that more helpful than simply a rehashing of the same sort of material at great expense of time and without the assistance of a document to help us all have it stick in the memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What are you seeking to establish, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to establish that as the witness indicated himself, he as an authorised official drafted certain documents, conducted interviews and so on, and based on that he was able to establish that the persons mentioned in Schedule A of Mr. Nice, that 30 of them out of 40 appear in his statements as members of the KLA. And during examination-in-chief, I provided that list to you in order to assist both you and Mr. Nice and make it possible for you to compare the names, draw charts, and see the tabs in which these names appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice -- I'm sorry. Mr. Milosevic, the question is being dealt with about this chart being offered by Mr. Nice, and I don't think you would agree with the comments made by the Prosecutor, but the note where these 30 people appear in what statements, as for that I don't think you have any opposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Haven't you already dealt with this matter in chief?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the examination-in-chief, it came out that out of 40 persons found in the mosque, 30 of them were mentioned as members of the KLA in different documents of Mr. Jasovic. That is what was established. But during the cross-examination, Mr. Nice presented some statements that he compiled over the past several days where some of that is being challenged. Now, I would like to establish that even in these statements that were compiled in 2005 there are some things that are not challenged. Some names, rather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We have an exhibit which is D296, which I think you're referring to, which sets out the 30 names and the various documents that they're referred to. Now we have that. If the object is to show that in Mr. Nice's statements there is agreement with some of the material, then you would need to identify for the witness the statement you want him to look at, because I doubt if he's going to be in a position to pick out statements on the basis of a general question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Let us now have a look at this. I think Mr. Nice -- it says on the 26th of May, 2005. There is a facsimile of an Albanian book, the 26th of May. That's what it says here in the introductory part. "[In English] Pursuant to Rule 68 related to Kosovo." [Interpretation] Yes. And, inter alia -- well, there are a few things there in relation to Kotlina, some other parts, but there is the book there, KLA, that Mr. Nice did present here during his cross-examination, with KLA emblem. I don't have a translation here because the book was presented only in Albanian. However, names don't have to be translated. Could someone please be so kind as to remind me of the name of the book?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you referring to a book named "Phoenix"?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that's it. The front page is 00088063.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think the book is in translation titled "Fallen Heroes."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's the book that Ms. Anoya has now. Yes. All right. Could a copy of this book please be placed before the witness. I just need to say one more thing. This book certainly is not complete, and it is yet to be established what is missing. However, even this incomplete version of the book supplies sufficient information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasovic, did you manage to open the book?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have the book open here now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, please look at page 20.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see page 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Afrim Syla is the fifth name there, 1999, Racak.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Afrim Syla.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. It's in Albanian, and I don't know how to read Albanian. But is this one of the participants of Racak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says he was born in 1975 in the village of Racak, and he lost his life in Racak in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. That's what it says with regard to each and every individual that I'm going to draw your attention to. So do you know the name? They included it this book of theirs that they called "Fallen Heroes."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's not among the 30 names you gave?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's not among those names but I'd have to have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But they did put the name here. Now, please look to two pages on, page 22.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. Line 6, does it say Ahmet Kaciku, again, 1999 Racak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ahmet Kaciku, born in 1964, a member of the KLA. I have information about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. This is from their book?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I need to point out that this person was not among the bodies in the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And the next page, the second one from the bottom does it also say Racak, 1999, Ali R. Beqa?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ali R. Beqa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is he also in Racak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Lost his life in 1999 in Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. The following page, the fifth person on the list, again got killed in 1999 in Racak. That's what it says?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Alush Mustafa, 1999 in Racak. He was born in 1966.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now look at page 40.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found page 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The fifth person again Racak 1999; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Enver Rashiti. He appears as a member of the KLA in various statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what they say here, too, that he was killed in Racak.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But again he was not among the bodies found in Racak. In the mosque, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm having some trouble following the page references but I couldn't find that on page 40. Oh, up from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Page 40, the fifth name on the list. Again lost his life in Racak.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN JASOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fifth name from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Again, I'm sure the accused will have remembered as we spend time on this that so far as those who are named, if you turn to page 5 of the schedule, we've already identified those who appear in this book so far as we've been able to analyse it. There are three of them. And so far as other people are concerned, including those who on Shukri Buja's evidence were taken away, and there may be others, they are barely relevant. So that you have the three names here of those on the book. You can see, for example -- let me just identify the three ones so the accused follows it although I explained it earlier. If you work your way up from the bottom, one -- on page 5, turning the page on one, two, three, four, five, six, seven up you've got Osmani Sadik appears on the list of "Fallen Heroes." The next one up above that is Lufti Bilalli, three down from the top. And the third one is the top one, Bajrami Ragip. So those are the three who we've explained appear in this book. The accused is quite right that the book as apparently served under Rule 68, but as I have explained that was out of an abundance of generosity. It wasn't necessary to serve it under Rule 68, but nevertheless it was thought in the circumstances better to ensure he had a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
